Updated read-through incorporating Beige Book and SLOOS:

- Policy stance: The FOMC kept the target range at 5.25–5.50% and continued QT ($60B Treasuries, $35B agency MBS), emphasizing cumulative tightening, policy lags, and data dependence. Administered rates (IORB 5.4%, ON RRP 5.3%) and standing facilities signal a clearly restrictive, anti-inflationary stance.

- Beige Book confirmation of cooling momentum: Across Federal Reserve Districts, overall activity was flat to modest. Consumer spending was mixed with softer discretionary categories; manufacturing was flat-to-down; housing remained constrained by low inventories and high mortgage rates; and CRE—especially office—was weak. Labor demand eased with improved labor availability and moderating wage growth. Price increases continued to slow, though inflation remained above target. Banks reported weaker loan demand, tighter standards, higher funding costs, and intensified deposit competition—broadly consistent with tighter financial conditions.

- SLOOS alignment: The latest SLOOS showed tightening across C&I, CRE, RRE, and consumer credit, with weaker loan demand. These reinforce Beige Book reports of credit restraint and cautious bank risk appetite, particularly among smaller/regional banks.

- Implications: Beige Book + SLOOS corroborate the FOMC’s warning that tighter credit will weigh on activity and hiring while aiding disinflation. Residual banking-sector vulnerabilities (CRE concentrations, unrealized losses, deposit competition) and persistent policy restraint tilt near-term growth risks softer, while longer-run inflation credibility is supported.

Net tone shift: From slightly positive to moderately cautious on near-term growth/risk assets, while incrementally constructive for disinflation.
